Pakistan's bowling response was spearheaded by Shaheen Afridi (4/108), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Finishing at 431/10 (154.6 ov), New Zealand established an overwhelming first-innings foundation that firmly dictated the terms of the match.

scorecards.inningsCommentary: Pakistan embarked on a high-stakes fourth-innings chase of 373 Runs, confronting a deteriorating pitch and aggressive field settings. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 102 from Fawad Alam, complemented by a commanding 165-run stand between Mohammad Rizwan and Fawad Alam that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 2.17 RPO. Tim Southee (2/32) maintained tight lines for New Zealand, creating intermittent chances in an otherwise demanding fielding effort. Dismissed for 271/10 (123.3 ov), Pakistan succumbed to fourth-innings pressure as New Zealand's bowlers closed out the victory.

New Zealand's bowling attack dismantled Pakistan for 271 in the fourth innings to complete the win.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Bay Oval commenced with high tactical intensity as New Zealand posted 431/10 (154.6 ov) in their opening innings. In response, Pakistan countered with 239/10 (102.2 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during Century: Fawad Alam 102 (270b), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Kane Williamson delivered a masterclass for New Zealand (150 Runs), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (New Zealand 57%) and allowing New Zealand to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, Pakistan faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. New Zealand's bowling unit, bolstered by Faheem Ashraf (110 Runs & 1 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing New Zealand won by 101 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: New Zealand's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While Pakistan produced fighting phases, New Zealand won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
